subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should maintainers accept a shared SSRF dispatcher/socket-level fix for IPv6-only no-route failures now, and should the current linked PR be repaired or replaced?
rationale: The fix touches the SSRF security boundary and Undici dispatcher contracts, and the current linked PR has known safety/type issues rather than being a clean landing candidate.

options.title: Repair and prove the linked PR
options.body: Keep this issue open while the linked PR preserves explicit-proxy pinning, fixes Undici connector typing, and adds live/log proof for rejection without process exit.

options.title: Request a replacement PR
options.body: Close or pause the linked PR if its unrelated script/docs changes and connector approach are not worth repairing, then ask for a narrower SSRF-only patch.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Wait for a maintainer-run or reporter-provided IPv6-unreachable Docker proof before accepting any security-boundary code change.

recommendation.title: Repair and prove the linked PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while the linked PR preserves explicit-proxy pinning, fixes Undici connector typing, and adds live/log proof for rejection without process exit.

likelyOwner.reason: Most relevant history owner for the shared SSRF guard, explicit proxy pinning, and Undici dispatcher construction path.
